title: The Reckoning
sceneText:
After dark things stop, one at a time.

The people in the fields come back first. Then the light in the stable goes out. The kitchen holds on longest; Martha is clearing up, and she takes longer over it than usual.

In the office you finish the last page of the month’s accounts.

What is spread on the desk: the general ledger, the tenant roll, the felling record, the market receipts, the assessment of dues. And the copy of the guarantee, number VS-18-0947.

Thirty days ago you put your name to it.

variants.admitted: You said something on that street in Valehold. You have still not said it to a second person.
variants.review:
You set down on paper what you did this month. Not to account for it; the forms for accounting for it are already filled in. You only wanted to see what these thirty days actually held.

How many mornings of reaping. How many trips to market. How many households’ roofs mended. How many evenings in the stable, and how many nights you slept against the office desk.

The numbers come out smaller than you thought. Thirty days is not long.

Then you turn to the last page and look at tonight’s figures.
variants.settled:
There is grain enough for the winter, enough for the dues, enough to sow next year. There is a surplus in guldmark. Enough timber has been kept back for heating.

You close the ledger and lean back in the chair.

The fire in the stove is the one Martha fed at dusk, and it is still up. There is no moon. Frost has begun to settle on those few quilts in the yard — Elena put them out this morning and forgot to bring them in. Or perhaps she did not forget.

You sit for a long time.

Thirty days ago you got down from a two-wheeled cart, your luggage was set on the steps, and a man in his fifties said three words to you.

You do not know what tomorrow will be. But tonight this book balances.
variants.short:
You work the figures three times.

Three times the same.

It is not short by much. It is short by exactly the amount that one more morning spent on it a fortnight ago would have covered — and there is no fortnight ago now. There is only tonight.

You sit in the office and hear the stable door catch the wind somewhere off.

And then you think of somebody.

effects.logEntry: You had Gregor saddle a horse and rode for Millridge in the night.

choices.resultText:
You closed the ledger.

The figures are the figures. Nothing you do tonight will make them into different figures, except one thing, and you did not do it.

You sat in the dark office until very late.
